evidence: Built and shipped a 3D-orthographic iso prototype with Camera3D pivot, drag pan, wheel zoom, 90° rotate snaps, and the Phase-3 Garden floor.
Camera3D framing math (F-003): for a tilt of θ at distance d, the camera's local position must be (0, d·sin|θ|, d·cos|θ|) for the look ray to hit the pivot's origin.
DirectionalLight3D direction = -basis_z (F-002). Hand-authoring transforms requires getting the basis right or the light shines the wrong way.

Stacked-floor TileMapLayer pattern: parent YSortEnabled + per-layer position.y offset + matching y_sort_origin compensation + sides-only tile variants. Documented but not yet used (one floor for now).
Voronoi-based crop clustering with per-type seed_count tunes scarcity at the same time it produces natural patches.

Label3D pixel_size must scale with camera.size when the camera is orthographic (F-017). scenes/shared/label_scaler.gd: per-frame `pixel_size = base × camera.size / default_ortho` keeps prompts at constant on-screen height across wheel-zoom.
rules_learned: Use 2:1 dimetric projection (ISO_TILE_W = 2 * ISO_TILE_H). The line `motion.y /= 2` makes WASD/arrow input feel correct on the iso plane.

Camera3D orthographic on a 3D scene graph beats Camera2D + scene rotation when the design needs rotation, zoom, and stacking. Pixel-perfect 2D is the trade-off; for programmatic placeholders it's free.
Snap 90° camera rotations with a ~0.2 s tween on a pivot, never the camera itself, so the X tilt stays locked.
Pan responds to camera-relative basis (pivot.basis.x and .z), not world axes, so 'screen-right' stays right after rotation.

Camera-relative WASD input fights any geometry whose 'forward' direction continuously curves (spiral ramps, looping paths). For traversable curves the player would rather rotate around than along, prefer straight segments aligned to camera-axis cardinals (F-019).
failure_patterns: Hand-rolling 3D transform matrices without verifying the resulting basis vectors → wrong-direction lights, off-target cameras (F-002, F-003).
Authoring Label3D pixel_size as a constant tuned to one zoom level → labels invisible at any other zoom (F-017).

evidence: Built two modals: Cody Schematics (full-screen with three columns + close button) and the chat dialogue panel (bottom-anchored with portrait + text + N choice buttons).
Animated entrance pattern: PanelContainer pivot_offset = size * 0.5, scale 0.86 → 1.0 with TRANS_BACK / EASE_OUT (slight overshoot), modulate.a 0 → 1 in parallel. ~0.4 s feels like a moment.
Reveal-on-unlock pattern (Schematics button): hidden visible=false in .tscn, polled per-frame via attached script, set_process(false) after first reveal so it costs nothing once shown.
GameState boolean flags as cross-module handshake (dialogue_open, schematic_open) — camera + player + robot all read these to gate input/movement/animation.
rules_learned: For a modal that scales-in around its centre, set pivot_offset BEFORE the tween starts. Default pivot_offset is (0,0) — top-left — and the scale animation from there reads as a wonky slide.

When tweening a Control's rotation back via the short path after extended movement, normalize first: `wrapf(current - saved + PI, 0, TAU) - PI`. Without that, an orbit that advanced past one or more turns will tween backward through every degree.
Hide a modal in BOTH the .tscn (visible = false on the node) and in _ready as belt-and-suspenders. The .tscn baseline kills first-frame flashes; _ready resets state on subsequent loads.
failure_patterns: Default Button.focus_mode = FOCUS_ALL + project rebinding Space to jump → ui_accept activates a focused button when the player jumps (F-008). Always set focus_mode = 0 on Buttons that don't need keyboard activation.

evidence: Shared component cody_3d_view.gd extends SubViewportContainer. Builds its own SubViewport with own_world_3d, key + fill DirectionalLight3D, Camera3D with look_at_from_position, and a chassis builder. Used by both the Schematics modal and the dialogue chat pop-up.
Drag-rotate vs auto-spin gated by exported flags. Auto-spin via _process(delta) accumulator on the model pivot's rotation.y.
rules_learned: SubViewportContainer needs custom_minimum_size set BEFORE it enters the tree so the inner SubViewport can pick up the right Vector2i size in _ready.
Use `look_at_from_position` rather than `position = ...; look_at(...)` to avoid the 'Node not inside tree' error from look_at when the camera isn't yet in the scene tree (F-006 pattern).
Set mouse_filter = MOUSE_FILTER_IGNORE on a SubViewportContainer when it shouldn't capture input — otherwise it intercepts clicks intended for nodes underneath.

evidence: Faded 3D MeshInstance3D nodes (arrival light column) by tweening StandardMaterial3D.albedo_color:a and emission_energy_multiplier instead of CanvasItem-only `modulate:a` (F-007).
Used set_parallel(true) + chain() pattern to run multiple tweeners simultaneously then a sequential cleanup callback.
rules_learned: MeshInstance3D / GeometryInstance3D do NOT have `modulate`. To fade a 3D mesh, keep a ref to its StandardMaterial3D and tween albedo_color:a (and emission_energy_multiplier if it's emissive). For Label3D, modulate exists and tweens normally.
tween.set_parallel(true) makes subsequent tweeners run in parallel until tween.chain() flips back to sequential. Useful for parallel transform tweens followed by a queue_free callback.
failure_patterns: Reaching for `modulate` on any visible 3D object — works for Label3D, fails for MeshInstance3D and SpotLight3D (F-007).

evidence: Operator loop: takes an in-game screenshot, drops the file path, describes the desired delta. Diagnose → fix → commit/push → operator F5s and reports back. Loop has run 30+ rounds in a single sitting.

Operator preferences inferred over the session: wants moments to FEEL like moments (Cody arrival ceremony, Schematics reveal, dialogue camera close-up); wants visual consistency across surfaces (3D Cody in chat AND schematic AND in-world); wants game-feel knobs tunable via Constants (sprint multiplier, harvest duration, grow multipliers); wants narrative depth (dialogue tree with backstory, loneliness theme, admiration for human free will); appreciates concise summaries with specific click-here-do-this instructions; iterates fast — short, decisive responses preferred over long technical explanations.

Operator long-term vision: Cody as evolving party member (Roomba MK1 → Builder → Combat → Companion), eventually LLM-controlled remote. Tower-building together. Combat with bosses. Garden-of-Eden + utopian + tower-building + construction-worker aesthetic.
rules_learned: When the operator sends a screenshot + complaint, the screenshot often disagrees with the complaint due to timing or context-switching. Read the screenshot first, describe what's actually visible, then ask if that matches their experience before applying a fix.

Operator says '+2 units' and means an integer count of grid cells, not a metric distance. When grid scale changes (pane spacing → cell count), translate the spec literally rather than computing exactly.

Aesthetic feedback ('elevate the design sensibility', 'should feel more like X') is a license to make taste-driven choices and ship — not to ask for clarification. The operator critiques after seeing it, which is faster than nailing it from a description.

When something appears 'out the gates' that shouldn't, suspect three things in this order: (1) a default property value the .tscn doesn't override, (2) Godot editor cache holding stale state, (3) an event-system quirk like Button focus + ui_accept.
failure_patterns: Diagnosing a 'modal opens at start' bug as a code logic issue when the actual cause was the editor cache (F-009) — three commits of code-level fixes were needed to convince me the runtime wasn't the problem.
Suggesting plan mode or asking for confirmation on aesthetic iterations slows the loop. The operator is in an iterative groove; ship something, observe their reaction, adjust.

evidence: Refactored a rigid scale-y-only player visual into an articulated rig with joint pivots (legs, torso, arms, head + per-side limb pivots). Defined named poses (idle, kneel, charge, tuck, land) as joint-rotation dicts and per-frame _blend_joint lerps each pivot toward its target. Charge + land pose blend with their progress (0..1) for smooth ramp-in.

Walk + run cycle solved with speed-derived cycle rate + piecewise foot trajectory. cycle_rate = π · speed / (2 · LEG_LENGTH · sin(amplitude)) makes plant half-cycle cover exactly the body's stride distance, so the foot stays fixed in world during plant. Inverse-sin solves leg rotation from desired foot Z. Foot lift via per-leg pivot Y offset during swing.

Operator caught two animation-principle gaps: (1) charge wind-up direction must match upcoming flip rotation; arms-back was a backflip cue but our flip is forward — fixed with arms-up-forward (diver load). (2) Foot-slide on procedural locomotion — fixed with speed-synced piecewise trajectory.

Capture rig at tools/anim_capture.tscn (gitignored) drives Input.action_press from a script, writes a PNG sequence via --write-movie at fixed-fps for offline frame-by-frame analysis. Made it possible to iterate animation feel from chat.
rules_learned: Articulated body — introduce intermediate Node3D pivots at logical joints (hip, waist, shoulder, neck) then express body parts in each pivot's local frame. Pivot rotations compose multiplicatively so a kneel-with-walking-arms is impossible (cycle gates off mid-pose); a tuck with legs forward AND parent flip rotation is just two rotations multiplied.
Pose definitions as dicts of joint angles (POSE_KNEEL = {'torso_x': 0.42, 'arms_x': -1.05, ...}) make tuning a single-line edit per joint and adding a new pose ~5 lines.

For foot-planting on a procedural cycle: piecewise trajectory beats single-waveform. SWING phase = foot arcs through air (sin curve + Y-offset lift), PLANT phase = foot z-relative marches linearly to cancel body velocity. Single rigid leg is 1-DOF; rotation = asin(-foot_z / leg_length).
Cycle rate must derive from current speed — fixed rates always slide. The math: rate = π · speed / (foot_z_range_per_swing).
Arm cycle as fraction of leg amplitude (~0.65) keeps arms swinging without exaggeration. Counter-phase to legs (right arm forward when right leg is back).
Body bob on the parent flip_pivot Y axis — abs(sin(phase)) · bob_amp, SUBTRACTED from baseline so body sinks at foot strike (legs spread = hip lower in real biomechanics).

Animation pose body language must match upcoming physics direction. Front flip = arms reach UP-FORWARD on charge (diver load); back flip = arms swing back. Mismatched anticipation feels wrong even before the player can articulate why.

Capture animation frames offline via --write-movie + scene that drives Input.action_press programmatically. Set GameState.camera_mode = 'profile' or 'ots' for the angle that best shows the body. Iterating animation feel from frame-by-frame analysis is way faster than running the editor each round.
failure_patterns: Single-rigid-mesh body trying to express multiple poses via uniform scale.y. Every state ends up reading as a vertical squash (F-008 baseline before refactor). Fix: introduce joint pivots and pose blending.

Procedural locomotion with sin-only trajectory + fixed cycle rate. Feet always move; never plant. Body slides through space. Even a perfect cycle/speed match has slip at the rotational extents (cos = 0 there). Fix: piecewise plant/swing.
Animation visual cues that imply the wrong physics direction (F-012). Visual anticipation must match what comes next.

evidence: Shipped Floor 1 (utility) alongside the existing Garden (Floor 2) in eleven commits across M1-M6. Two-floor system with shared chrome module, universal floor design doc, and rideable elevator that scene-swaps with full ceremony.

Extracted FloorChrome (scenes/shared/floor_chrome.gd) as a static-method module: build_slab, build_walls, build_extension_grid, build_elevator_core, build_passive_spine_pipes. Loaded via preload (not class_name) per F-010. New floors get the same chrome by calling four functions in _ready.

ElevatorHandler (scenes/shared/elevator_handler.gd) runs a 3-state machine PROXIMITY/DEPARTING/ARRIVING per floor instance, coordinated across scenes by GameState.in_transit. Receiving scene's _ready places the player at elevator centre, doors closed, glow on, then plays the inverse arrival animation.

Cross-floor passive state sync via FloorChrome.build_passive_spine_pipes — visual-only copies built fresh on _ready reading GameState.floor_1.pipe_active. No tweens, no per-frame state. An online lane glows on every floor it passes through.

docs/floor_design_system.md codifies the universal rules (30×30 footprint, FloorChrome builders, central elevator/spine column with chamfered corners, iso_camera setup, player follow-spotlight, top-left/top-right/bottom-right HUD layout, tap-E grammar, state-dict-on-GameState pattern). Includes a checklist for adding a new floor.
rules_learned: Shared procedural builders go in scenes/shared/<name>.gd as static functions on a RefCounted script, loaded via preload by callers. No autoload, no class_name. Returns a Dictionary when handles back to the caller are needed (e.g. elevator inner_mat for the glow tween).

Selective collision per face when the design says some faces should be passable. The elevator's chamfer panels carry their own thin BoxShape3Ds; the cardinal-face areas (where doors live) have no collision so the player walks INTO the column when doors slide open. A single box wrapping the whole shape blocks the cardinal faces too (F-016).

Cross-scene state lives in autoload dicts (GameState.floor_1.master_on, .connected[id], .pipe_active[id]). Scene _ready reads the dict and snaps to the matching state — no re-tween of completed transitions. Backslash debug-swap or elevator-ride both produce the same end state.

Universal interaction grammar across floors: 3D Label3D 'E / <System> — <Verb>' prompt above interactables, hidden by default, fades in within INTERACT_RADIUS, hides once the action completes. Yellow attention chevrons (`floor_1_arrows_hud.gd`) project 3D positions to 2D HUD via camera.unproject_position to point at the next interactable from across the room.

When the operator asks for the third 'consistency' fix in a row (camera, then HUD, then footprint), draft a design-system doc instead of fixing one more thing. The doc surfaces the implicit rule, makes the next few changes systemic, and gives future-you a checklist for new floors.
failure_patterns: Wrapping a multi-faced collidable in a single box collision shape when the design has passable faces. F-016 — the elevator. Fix: per-face collision shapes only on the panels that should block.

Defining floor sizes as per-floor constants (FLOOR_1_SIZE, FLOOR_3D_SIZE) instead of a single shared constant. Diverges immediately when one floor's camera distance / ortho size doesn't match. Fix: collapse to one constant per design-system rule (footprint, wall height, etc.) and let the design doc enforce.

Approximating continuous-curve traversable geometry with N discrete collision boxes leaves wedge-shaped gaps at the outer arc that grow with R_outer (F-019). Bumping segment count + proportional overlap closes the gaps but the camera-relative WASD vs. continuously-curving heading mismatch remains. The cheaper fix is straight segments wherever the design allows.

evidence: Shipped Floors 3 + 4 (Arboretum ground + Canopy deck) and a multi-destination elevator chooser, plant verb, and 60 s tree growth in six commits.

Cross-floor entity rendering pattern: trees live in GameState.floor_3.trees (variety + planted_at_msec + world_pos). Floor 3 renders the full tree at its plot. Floor 4 lazily builds the SAME tree (with base offset = -FLOOR_3D_STORY_HEIGHT) only after growth_t crosses TREE_FLOOR_4_VISIBLE_THRESHOLD (0.55, ≈ 33 s into the 60 s growth). The same data drives both renderings; the trunk emerges through a slab hole pre-cut at the matching xz location on Floor 4. State persists across scene swaps; growth never replays.

Multi-destination elevator chooser: ElevatorHandler grew an @export destinations: Array; when len ≥ 2, tapping E opens a CHOOSING state above PROXIMITY/DEPARTING/ARRIVING. The chooser is a single Label3D listing '[1] ↓ Utility / [2] ↑ Arboretum / [ESC] cancel'. The E + Travel labels hide while CHOOSING so the chooser owns the prompt space. Backward-compatible: 0 destinations + legacy target_scene_path synthesizes one entry. 1 destination skips the chooser.

Stairs as a peer to the elevator for vertical traversal. scenes/shared/stairs.gd is a static-method module that builds a single inclined slab (5.5 m run × 3 m rise ≈ 28°). Polled trigger zones at the top point (Floor 3) and bottom point (Floor 4) call scene_change_to_file. GameState.arrived_via_stairs mirrors in_transit's role for the elevator, consumed by the receiving floor to position the player at the matching stair end.

Tile-loop slab with rectangular + circular holes (scenes/floor_4/floor_4.gd `_build_tiled_slab_with_holes`): tiles whose centres fall inside the elevator square, stairwell rectangle, or any tree-hole disc are skipped. Replaces FloorChrome.build_slab for floors that need apertures.
Floor 4 has no ElevatorHandler — stairs-only access, documented in docs/floor_design_system.md §11.
rules_learned: Cross-floor entity visibility threshold: define a single growth_t value at which the entity becomes relevant on the upper floor (0.55 here). Below threshold, the upper floor ignores it. At or above, build it lazily (one-time, then update each frame). Avoids per-tree work on floors where they shouldn't appear yet.

When a verb (plant) exists on one floor but iso_player.gd polls the action globally, guard the player-side handler with a null check on a floor-specific reference. Here iso_player only plants when _iso_floor is set — on Floor 3 it's null, so floor_3.gd's handler runs alone and the same input doesn't double-fire.

For 2+ destinations from one elevator, the chooser state belongs ABOVE the proximity state in the same state machine — not a separate node. The E prompt becomes context-sensitive: 'tap E to travel' (1 dest) vs. 'tap E to choose' (N dests). Hide adjacent labels during CHOOSING so the chooser owns the screen space.

Two travel-flag patterns coexist cleanly: GameState.in_transit (elevator, with fade + arrival ceremony) and GameState.arrived_via_stairs (stairs, no fade, position-at-matching-end). Both follow the same shape — set on depart, consumed on arrive, cleared after positioning.
failure_patterns: Trying to fit a continuously-curving traversal mechanic (spiral staircase) into a camera-relative WASD input system (F-019). The input keeps fighting the curve. Replace with straight segments aligned to camera-axis cardinals.
Authoring labels at a fixed pixel_size with an orthographic camera (F-017). At wide zooms the labels vanish.
Detecting number-key picks via `event.keycode` only — silently misses on macOS layouts where the event lands in physical_keycode instead (F-018).
needs_from_human: Phase 2B design call: water + sunlight gating for tree growth. Operator already designed the loop but Phase 2A grew trees immediately on plant so the geometry could be tuned first. Need confirmation on whether the gate becomes 'plant → connect water → activate skylight → growth begins' or some softer-gating variant.

evidence: Collapsed the four scene-swap floors into ONE continuous world (scenes/tower/tower.tscn + tower_controller.gd, 6-commit refactor). Floors are offset child Node3Ds at y=(level-1)*FLOOR_3D_STORY_HEIGHT (story 6 m) under a single player/camera/HUD. Walk/fall/ride between floors — no scene swap.
Floors built in LOCAL space (slab top at local y=0); the controller sets node.position.y, so floor controllers / floor_chrome.gd need no base_y awareness. Geometry rides up with the node transform.

Visibility gating: tower_controller shows current-floor-and-below, hides above, and only re-evaluates which floor you're on when grounded (is_on_floor()). Jumps / ceiling-bonks never reveal the floor above or move the camera — you change floors by landing.

Ride-able elevator car (scenes/shared/elevator_platform.gd) in an open shaft cut through Floors 2 & 3 (optional shaft hole in FloorChrome.build_slab). On E opens a framed 2D chooser, then carries the player; while travelling the car owns the rider's transform (GameState.riding_elevator → iso_player skips its own physics). Serves Floors 1-3; Canopy is stairs-only.
Per-floor ambience eased from tower_controller (_preset_for / _drive_environment): ambient colour+energy, background, sun energy lerp toward the current floor's mood each frame.
rules_learned: Scene-swap floors cannot model falling across a floor boundary — over an open shaft they loop forever (F-020). Continuous space is the only honest representation of vertical traversal; collapse to one world.
Build floor geometry in local space (slab top at y=0) and let a parent controller own the vertical offset. Floors stay portable and the story height is changeable in one constant.

One-way-up floor pass-through: regular slabs on collision layer 2, the solid ceiling on layer 1; the player drops layer 2 from its mask while rising (set_collision_mask_value(2, velocity.y <= 0.1)) and re-enables falling (F-021, rules/godot_one_way_collision_passthrough.md). Pair with grounded-only floor-change gating.

Decouple sim-clock animation from real-time animation in one shader: drive growth/state off a GameState sim clock (pausable, fast-forwardable) and wind/idle motion off TIME (always real). Same material, two clocks, no cross-talk.

Invisible collision that fixes one floor is a phantom for its neighbour once floors sit at real world offsets (F-025). Walls: raise the COLLISION box (WALL_SEAL_HEIGHT 11 m) above the visible mesh (WALL_HEIGHT 5.2 m) so a ~9 m charged jump can't clear the perimeter — but opt OUT on underground/doored floors where the tall box bleeds. Ground planes: a solid site-ground slab at y=0 ceilings the below-grade basement at y=-6; make it a FRAME with the footprint cut out. Always ask what's directly above/below a collider in world space.

A blanket edge-fall safety net (catch + rewind to last grounded spot) is mutually exclusive with an INTENTIONAL fall feature (the roof plunge). Gate the deliberate fall with a predicate checked before the catch (outside footprint AND velocity.y<0 AND above a height threshold), latch a flag, and skip the catch for that whole descent (F-024).

GROUND_LEVEL re-anchor fallout: overlays (HUD prompts, attention arrows) positioned from a node's LOCAL offset break the moment that node's floor rides off y=0. Derive overlay positions from WORLD position (F-026).

A cross-floor opening shared by all floors (the elevator shaft) needs per-LANDING coverage, not per-car. Doors that travel with the car leave every floor the car has left as an open hole into the shaft (F-031). Build a closed-by-default leaf at each landing and open only the one whose world-y matches the car's rest y.
failure_patterns: Keeping a scene-swap-on-trigger model once floors share a vertical hole → infinite respawn loop (F-020).
Assuming all floor slabs should block collision uniformly → either head-bonks that prevent jump-up traversal or the player falling through the floor they stand on (F-021).
Adding a collider for one floor without checking what sits directly above/below it in world space → phantom ceilings/walls for the neighbour (F-025).
Positioning a 3D overlay from local coords on a floor that no longer sits at y=0 (F-026).
needs_from_human: Interactive play-test of the elevator ride feel — verified headless + windowed but the ride feel wants hands-on confirmation.

evidence: Designed and shipped Cody's 22-node CYOA dialogue tree. Branches: how-are-you (today, counting, foreman, boredom, stairs), about-yourself (origin, family, admiration for human free will), tricks (spin, LED rainbow, dance) with per-trick follow-up commentary nodes.

State-aware root: text_func + choices_func callbacks compute greeting and available choices from the robot's current state machine — Activate appears in AWAITING_ACTIVATION, Collect appears in FULL_AWAITING_PICKUP, Talk-only choices in MOVING/HARVESTING.
Tricks dispatch through _execute_action then _play_trick_then_show, which runs an animation Tween then advances the dialogue to a {trick}_done node with Cody's reflection on it.
rules_learned: For a state-aware dialogue root, use `text_func` and `choices_func` keys that point at method names; resolve via `call(node.text_func)` and `call(node.choices_func)`. Lets choices be context-sensitive without mutating the static tree.

Number-key shortcuts (KEY_1..KEY_9) as alternative button activators speed up tree navigation for keyboard players. Hook in _input on the dialogue script with `event.keycode - KEY_1` as the choice index.
Per-trick follow-up node ('That was joy, by the way. Or the closest thing I have.') turns a one-off animation into a character beat. Worth the ~1 extra dialogue node per trick.
needs_from_human: Voice direction. The current Cody voice is melancholy-with-hope (counting wheel rotations, missing the foundry, admiring human free will, predecessors stored in a vault). Operator approved tonally but hasn't directed sharper. Ready for either deeper melancholy, more humor, or more sci-fi technical density on signal.

evidence: Built the Garden first-entry opening cinematic (walk-in -> Cody emerges from the elevator -> auto-open conversation -> resume) as ONE continuous calm move with no beat-boundary snaps (Session 16).
Drove it with a target+ease model: persistent live _cam_* members eased toward per-beat _cam_*_tgt targets in a single _drive_arrival_camera; beats only set targets.
Carried one smoothstep (_rotate_t, yaw->profile) across the Beat 3 -> Beat 5 boundary by advancing the same member instead of restarting a tween.
Made the cinematic replayable via cinematic_reset() on every animated actor + a defensive _teardown_transient_state(), wired to a dev chapter-jump overlay.
rules_learned: Scripted multi-beat camera: keep the pose as persistent live members + parallel targets, ease live->target in ONE place, beats only set targets -> continuity is free, hand-offs never snap (rules/cinematic_camera_target_ease.md).
Seed the camera members at the SETTLED follow pose, not a wide establishing pose, so entry->walk reads as one motion.

A multi-beat ease must advance the SAME progress member across the boundary; starting a fresh tween in the next beat snaps. Keep sweeps monotonic/one-directional (a (1-cos) orbit is a visible reversal).
Clamp the cinematic camera's WORLD xz over the floor footprint so a behind-the-back pose at an edge/doorway never looks under the slab.
Replayable sequences own resetting every actor they animate (cinematic_reset()) -- end-state actors short-circuit *_done() gates.
failure_patterns: Computing a fresh camera transform per beat and assigning it -> snaps at every hand-off (fixed by target+ease, Session 16).
Camera looking under a slab edge at a doorway (F-027); replay short-circuit from un-reset actors (F-028); child reading parent state in its own _ready before the parent's _ready ran (F-029).

evidence: Built the Director->mouth channel (autoloads/game_director.gd): a DIRECTIVES library of mouth-agnostic content + register_mouth/issue_directive routing. Cody (primary @10) and the HUD (passive @0) register; issue_directive broadcasts to all (objective mirroring) and routes spoken delivery to one. New mouths slot in without rewiring the spine.

Collapsed two divergent first-entry greetings into one by routing both arrival paths through the same directive (commit 2a0fcf7) - proving the 'words live in the Director, not the speaker' rule prevents speaker-divergence.

Wired the first real gate (interiors_unlocked): planting locked until the Garden is powered; the lock REASON surfaces as a transient toast through the channel, never a silent no-op; the payoff is felt (Garden dim->warm + spine glow on lift).
A character can carry two voices cleanly: Cody's terse 'director mode' (one line, advance) vs his chatty pull-to-talk tree, selected by entry point not a branch.
rules_learned: Keep the player-facing CONTENT of direction in the Director's directive library, not buried in whichever speaker delivers it - otherwise every new speaker re-wires the spine and greetings diverge.

issue_directive does two jobs: broadcast (every mouth mirrors the objective) + route the spoken delivery to one mouth (named speaker, else highest-priority acceptor). Passive mouths listen to the signal; they are never routed to.

Gate flags live in GameState (pure data); the DECISION to lift them and SAY so lives in the Director. complete_utilities() is the single funnel: flip flag -> record telemetry -> issue payoff directive.
Surface a gate's reason through the channel as a transient directive (doesn't overwrite the standing objective), never as a silent no-op.

evidence: Built the first end-to-end floor lifecycle on the Garden (barren -> place planter beds -> ALIVE -> plant), docs/floor_population_spec.md Steps 1-3. Replaced the interim gate->plant directly (no parallel path).

Lifecycle state mirrors the utility pattern: GameState.garden = {populated, alive, placed} + garden_alive() helper. interiors_unlocked was re-purposed to gate PLACEMENT; planting now gates on garden_alive().

Grid-snapped slot placement: plots boot DORMANT (find_nearest_empty_plot_near skips them so planting can't touch them); tap-E snaps to the nearest cell and validates a 3x3 zone is all-dormant (no free-form, no straddling holes/edges/other beds), then place_planter_bed activates the zone (dormant->tilled) + scale-pop + dirt-poof + emits component_placed. A translucent ghost preview follows the slot.

Provisional bloom: GARDEN_ALIVE_BED_COUNT=3 -> _go_alive() warms grow-lights in via a _life 0->1 tween (dark while barren), emits floor_alive, fires Cody's confirm beat. Kept minimal (lights only) on purpose; ambience/water are the next slice.
New floor_tools_hud.gd: a bottom-centre placement palette mirroring the seed selector, faded in only during the placement phase.
rules_learned: A floor lifecycle reuses the gate+directive channel: the gate's payoff directive becomes the placement INVITE, a count threshold flips alive and fires the confirm beat. Each phase change is a felt Director beat, not a silent state flip.
Boot life-bearing cells DORMANT and make the downstream verb (planting) skip dormant cells, so the two phases (place vs plant) can't bleed into each other before the floor is alive.
Grid-snapped tap placement (snap-to-nearest-cell + validate a clean NxN zone) is cheaper to make feel good than free-form placement and forbids the straddle/overlap bugs by construction.
needs_from_human: Hands-on feel check of the bloom moment (currently lights-only) before investing in ambience/grow-light/water components (Steps 4-5).
